# index.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# ideadump

A place to dump ideas: capture them in your own words, research them a little, index and relate them, and find them again.

```bash
pip install ideadump
```

You tell an agent an idea in passing; it runs one command to keep it, verbatim, and a light research pass to see what it is called, what already exists and whether it is promising. Later you ask what ideas you have about something, or whether anything you have been working on relates to them.

```bash
ideadump add "a place to dump ideas, and do a bit of research on them" --title "Idea dump" --tags "tools, notes" --source my-session
ideadump note idea-dump --file light-research.md --depth light     # attach research notes
ideadump find "note taking research"                                # ranked, with the shared words
ideadump find --file recent-work.md                                 # which ideas relate to this page of recent work?
ideadump ls --status promising
ideadump show idea-dump
```

Research is done by the agent with whatever search tools it has, so it sends queries (generic terms, not your notes) to outside services; the ideas themselves stay in your store.

The primary user is an agent: the package ships a skill, `ideadump`, that tells it when and how to use these verbs (capture, light and deep research, linking, the “is my recent work related to my ideas” pass). See [Agent skill]().

## Where ideas live

Ideas are kept in a [dol](https://github.com/i2mint/dol) store, a `MutableMapping` of path to text. By default it is a local folder, `~/.local/share/ideadump` (or `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`). Each idea is a folder:

```default
README.md                         # the index: newest first, then by tag (generated)
ideas/2026-11-14-idea-dump/
    idea.json                     # the record: words (verbatim), title, summary, tags, status, research, links
    README.md                     # the idea's page (generated)
    research/2026-11-14-light.md  # research notes, never overwritten
```

The pages are generated from the records on every write, so the folder reads well in a file browser or on GitHub.

### Syncing to a private git repository

```bash
pip install 'ideadump[git]'
ideadump sync-init you/my-ideas     # creates the repository PRIVATE if missing, and makes the data folder its checkout
ideadump sync                              # pull, commit everything, push
ideadump sync-status
```

The git work is [acquaint](https://github.com/thorwhalen/acquaint)’s guarded sync: it refuses a repository that is not private, and a pre-push hook re-checks the remote and its visibility on every push. `sync-init` adopts an existing ideas folder (and refuses one that is a checkout of another repository); on a second machine, clone the repository into the data folder first. Generated pages are marked in `.gitattributes` so they never conflict: `sync` rebuilds them from the merged records after each rebase. A private repository is access control, not encryption.

## Python

Every verb is a plain function returning a JSON-able dict, and takes the store as `files`, so any `MutableMapping` works (a `dict` in tests, another `dol` store elsewhere):

```python
from ideadump import add, find, note

files = {}
r = add("offline speech to text on the phone", tags="audio", files=files)
note(r["id"], text="# Prior art\n\nWhisper.cpp, Vosk.", files=files)
find("speech recognition", files=files)["hits"]
```

`find` ranks with BM25 (standard library); pass `score=` to plug in another scorer, such as a semantic one.

## Agent skill

The skill lives in the package at `ideadump/data/skills/ideadump/SKILL.md`. For Claude Code, with the package installed, link it into your skills folder:

```bash
ln -s "$(python -c 'import ideadump, pathlib; print(pathlib.Path(ideadump.__file__).parent / "data/skills/ideadump")')" ~/.claude/skills/ideadump
```

Then tell any session “idea for later: …” and it captures it. Other agent hosts read the same file; point yours at that folder (with the `gh skill` extension, `gh skill install thorwhalen/ideadump ideadump`).

# ideadump.base

Errors and constants shared across ideadump.

An idea is one folder in the store, `ideas/<id>/`, holding its record
(`idea.json`, the single source of truth), a rendered `README.md` that a person
reads on GitHub or a phone, and its research notes under `research/`. Nothing here
depends on any other module.

### Module Attributes

| [`STATUSES`](_autosummary/ideadump.base.html.md#ideadump.base.STATUSES)   | Where an idea stands.          |
|-------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| [`DEPTHS`](_autosummary/ideadump.base.html.md#ideadump.base.DEPTHS)     | How deep a research note went. |

### Functions

| [`record_key`](_autosummary/ideadump.base.html.md#ideadump.base.record_key)(idea_id)   | The store key of an idea's record.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|

### Exceptions

| [`IdeadumpError`](_autosummary/ideadump.base.html.md#ideadump.base.IdeadumpError)   | An error whose message says what to do next.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------|

### ideadump.base.DEPTHS *= ('light', 'deep')*

How deep a research note went. `light` is the pass made at capture (minutes, a
few sources); `deep` is a full `do-research`-style report.

### *exception* ideadump.base.IdeadumpError

Bases: [`Exception`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/exceptions.html#Exception)

An error whose message says what to do next.

### ideadump.base.STATUSES *= ('new', 'promising', 'parked', 'pursued', 'dropped')*

Where an idea stands. `new` on capture; the owner (or an agent relaying the
owner’s words) moves it on. `promising` is the cue for a deeper research pass.

### ideadump.base.record_key(idea_id)

The store key of an idea’s record.

```pycon
>>> record_key("2026-11-14-an-idea")
'ideas/2026-11-14-an-idea/idea.json'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/ideadump.html.md

# ideadump

ideadump: a place to dump ideas, research them a little, and find them again.

Capture an idea in the owner’s own words, attach research notes (a light pass at
capture, a deep one when it looks promising), tag and link ideas, and ask which ideas
relate to a query or to a page describing recent work. Ideas live in a `dol` store,
by default a local folder, optionally a checkout of a private git repository.

```pycon
>>> from ideadump import add, find
>>> files = {}
>>> _ = add("Offline speech to text on the phone", tags="audio", files=files)
>>> find("speech recognition", files=files)["hits"][0]["tags"]
['audio']
```

The command line (`ideadump --help`) and the agent skill shipped in
`ideadump/data/skills/ideadump` drive the same verbs.

### Functions

|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/ideadump.html.md#ideadump.data_dir)([data_dir])                               | The data root: the argument, else `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`, else the user data folder.                  |

### ideadump.add(words, , title=None, summary=None, tags=None, source=None, status='new', files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Capture an idea: the owner’s words verbatim, plus an optional title, summary and tags.

`words` is kept exactly as given (dictation slips included); put the cleaned-up
reading in `summary`. `tags` is comma-separated. `source` says where it was
captured (a session name, “phone”). Returns the new id.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.data_dir(data_dir=None)

The data root: the argument, else `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`, else the user data folder.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ideadump.find(query=None, , file=None, limit=10, files=None, data_dir=None, score=None)

Ideas related to a query, best first: a few words, or a page of text in `file`.

For “is anything I’ve been working on related to my ideas?”, put a description of
recent work (ledgers, issue titles, commit subjects) in a file and pass `--file`.
Each hit lists the words it shares with the query, so a weak match is visible.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.link(idea, other, , why=None, files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Relate two ideas, both ways, with an optional one-line reason.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.ls(, tag=None, status=None, limit=50, files=None, data_dir=None)

The ideas, newest first, optionally only those with a tag or a status.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.note(idea, , text=None, file=None, depth='light', title=None, files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Attach a research note (Markdown) to an idea, from `text` or a `file` path.

`depth` is `light` (the quick pass at capture) or `deep` (a full report).
Notes are never overwritten: a second note the same day gets its own file.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

One idea: its record, and the text of its page (words, summary, research, links).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.sync(, message=None, data_dir=None)

Commit every change in the data root, rebase onto the remote, push (no-op when not a git checkout).

Refuses while any record does not parse. After the rebase the pages are
regenerated from the merged records and pushed again if they changed.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Make the data root a checkout of the private GitHub repository `repo` (owner/name).

Creates the repository, private, when it does not exist; refuses one that is not
private. An existing ideas folder is adopted (committed and pushed); a folder that
is already a checkout of a different repository is refused.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/ideadump.render.html.md

# ideadump.render

Markdown views of the records: one `README.md` per idea and an index at the root.

The records (`idea.json`) are the source of truth; these pages are regenerated from
them on every write, so a person browsing the store on GitHub (or a phone) sees each
idea’s folder open on its page, and the root opens on the index.

### Functions

| [`idea_page`](_autosummary/ideadump.render.html.md#ideadump.render.idea_page)(record, \*[, titles])   | The page of one idea: the owner's words, the summary, research and links.      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`index_page`](_autosummary/ideadump.render.html.md#ideadump.render.index_page)(records)               | The root index: every idea, newest first, then the ideas under each tag.       |
| [`research_depth`](_autosummary/ideadump.render.html.md#ideadump.render.research_depth)(record)            | How far an idea has been researched: `deep`, `light` or `-`.                   |
| [`created_at`](_autosummary/ideadump.render.html.md#ideadump.render.created_at)(record)                | When an idea was captured, comparable across machines in different time zones. |

### ideadump.render.created_at(record)

When an idea was captured, comparable across machines in different time zones.

```pycon
>>> a = {"created": "2026-11-14T23:30:00+01:00"}
>>> b = {"created": "2026-11-14T22:45:00+00:00"}
>>> created_at(a) < created_at(b)
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`datetime`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/datetime.html#datetime.datetime)

### ideadump.render.idea_page(record, , titles=None)

The page of one idea: the owner’s words, the summary, research and links.

```pycon
>>> page = idea_page({"id": "x", "title": "T", "words": "w", "created": "2026-11-14"})
>>> page.splitlines()[0]
'# T'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ideadump.render.index_page(records)

The root index: every idea, newest first, then the ideas under each tag.

```pycon
>>> print(index_page([]).splitlines()[0])
# Ideas
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### ideadump.render.research_depth(record)

How far an idea has been researched: `deep`, `light` or `-`.

# _autosummary/ideadump.search.html.md

# ideadump.search

Rank ideas against a query: BM25 over words, standard library only.

The query can be a few words (“offline speech to text”) or a page of text describing
recent work (ledgers, issue titles, commit messages): long queries are the “is
anything I’ve been working on related to my ideas?” case. The scorer is a seam: any
`score(query, docs) -> list[float]` can be passed to [`rank()`](_autosummary/ideadump.search.html.md#ideadump.search.rank), for instance a
semantic scorer backed by the fleet’s `ir` search.

```pycon
>>> docs = {"a": "offline speech to text on a phone", "b": "a recipe for bread"}
>>> [hit["id"] for hit in rank("speech recognition offline", docs)]
['a']
```

### Functions

| [`tokens`](_autosummary/ideadump.search.html.md#ideadump.search.tokens)(text)                          | Lowercased content words of `text`, with a light plural fold.                  |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`bm25`](_autosummary/ideadump.search.html.md#ideadump.search.bm25)(query, docs, \*[, k1, b])        | BM25 score of each document for `query` (query terms counted once each).       |
| [`rank`](_autosummary/ideadump.search.html.md#ideadump.search.rank)(query, docs, \*[, limit, score]) | The ids of `docs` that match `query`, best first, with score and shared terms. |

### ideadump.search.bm25(query, docs, , k1=1.5, b=0.75)

BM25 score of each document for `query` (query terms counted once each).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### ideadump.search.rank(query, docs, \*, limit=10, score=<function bm25>)

The ids of `docs` that match `query`, best first, with score and shared terms.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

### ideadump.search.tokens(text)

Lowercased content words of `text`, with a light plural fold.

```pycon
>>> tokens("The ideas, and an Idea!")
['idea', 'idea']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md

# ideadump.store

Where ideas live: a `MutableMapping` of `/`-separated path to text.

Every verb takes a `files` store, so the default local folder can be swapped for any
other `dol` store (or a plain `dict` in tests) without touching the rest. The
default is a folder, the data root:

1. the `data_dir` argument, else
2. `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`, else
3. `~/.local/share/ideadump` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%` honoured).

To keep ideas in a private git repository, make the data root a checkout of it with
`ideadump sync-init <owner>/<name>` (see [`ideadump.sync`](_autosummary/ideadump.html.md#ideadump.sync)); the store
itself does not change.

```pycon
>>> data_dir("somewhere").is_absolute()
True
```

### Functions

| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md#ideadump.store.data_dir)([data_dir])                 | The data root: the argument, else `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`, else the user data folder.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`text_files`](_autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md#ideadump.store.text_files)(root)                     | A `dol` files store under `root`: `/`-separated keys, UTF-8 text values.             |
| [`resolve_files`](_autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md#ideadump.store.resolve_files)([files, data_dir_])    | `files` if given, else the text store over the data root.                            |
| [`writing`](_autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md#ideadump.store.writing)([files, data_dir_, timeout]) | The store, held exclusively while a verb reads, changes and rewrites it.             |

### ideadump.store.data_dir(data_dir=None)

The data root: the argument, else `$IDEADUMP_DATA_DIR`, else the user data folder.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### ideadump.store.resolve_files(files=None, , data_dir_=None)

`files` if given, else the text store over the data root.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ideadump.store.text_files(root)

A `dol` files store under `root`: `/`-separated keys, UTF-8 text values.

Folders are made on write and never on read; a delete is permanent.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### ideadump.store.writing(files=None, , data_dir_=None, timeout=30.0)

The store, held exclusively while a verb reads, changes and rewrites it.

Several sessions may capture ideas at the same moment; each write verb reads every
record, picks a free id, and rewrites the index, so two of them interleaving would
lose an idea. For the default folder store this takes a lock file in the data root
(created exclusively, so it works on every platform); a store passed in by the
caller is the caller’s to serialise.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterator)[[`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]


# _autosummary/ideadump.tools.html.md

# ideadump.tools

The verbs: plain functions, JSON-able arguments in, JSON-able dicts out.

This module is the single source of truth for what ideadump does; the command line
(`ideadump.__main__`) and the shipped agent skill are views of the list
`TOOLS`. Every verb takes a `files` store (see [`ideadump.store`](_autosummary/ideadump.store.html.md#module-ideadump.store)), so

```pycon
>>> files = {}
>>> r = add("Maybe a tool to dump ideas into, with a bit of research", title="Idea dump",
...         tags="tools, notes", files=files, now="2026-11-14T10:00:00+01:00")
>>> r["id"]
'2026-11-14-idea-dump'
>>> sorted(files)
['README.md', 'ideas/2026-11-14-idea-dump/README.md', 'ideas/2026-11-14-idea-dump/idea.json']
>>> find("research tool for ideas", files=files)["hits"][0]["id"]
'2026-11-14-idea-dump'
```

Verbs never print and never exit; each result carries a `text` field, the human
rendering, which the command line prints.

### Functions

| [`add`](_autosummary/ideadump.tools.html.md#ideadump.tools.add)(words, \*[, title, summary, tags, ...])        | Capture an idea: the owner's words verbatim, plus an optional title, summary and tags.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### ideadump.tools.add(words, , title=None, summary=None, tags=None, source=None, status='new', files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Capture an idea: the owner’s words verbatim, plus an optional title, summary and tags.

`words` is kept exactly as given (dictation slips included); put the cleaned-up
reading in `summary`. `tags` is comma-separated. `source` says where it was
captured (a session name, “phone”). Returns the new id.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.find(query=None, , file=None, limit=10, files=None, data_dir=None, score=None)

Ideas related to a query, best first: a few words, or a page of text in `file`.

For “is anything I’ve been working on related to my ideas?”, put a description of
recent work (ledgers, issue titles, commit subjects) in a file and pass `--file`.
Each hit lists the words it shares with the query, so a weak match is visible.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.link(idea, other, , why=None, files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Relate two ideas, both ways, with an optional one-line reason.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.ls(, tag=None, status=None, limit=50, files=None, data_dir=None)

The ideas, newest first, optionally only those with a tag or a status.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.note(idea, , text=None, file=None, depth='light', title=None, files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Attach a research note (Markdown) to an idea, from `text` or a `file` path.

`depth` is `light` (the quick pass at capture) or `deep` (a full report).
Notes are never overwritten: a second note the same day gets its own file.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.reindex(, files=None, data_dir=None)

Regenerate every idea page and the root index from the records.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.show(idea, , files=None, data_dir=None)

One idea: its record, and the text of its page (words, summary, research, links).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.update(idea, , title=None, summary=None, tags=None, add_tags=None, status=None, files=None, data_dir=None, now=None)

Change an idea’s title, summary, status, or tags (`tags` replaces, `add_tags` adds).

The owner’s words are never edited; the id never changes.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.where(, data_dir=None)

Where the ideas are stored, and whether that folder is synced to a git repository.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### ideadump.tools.without(func, hidden=('files', 'data_dir', 'now'))

The same verb with `hidden` parameters removed from its signature (for the CLI).

```pycon
>>> "files" in inspect.signature(without(show)).parameters
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`ideadump` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `ideadump`

Capture an idea the owner tells you, in their own words, research it a little (more if it looks promising), tag and link it, and find it again later, with the ideadump command. Use whenever the owner shares an idea unrelated to the current task or asks you to keep one (“I have an idea”, “idea:”, “jot this down”, “dump this idea”, “note this idea for later”, “remind me of this idea”), asks about their ideas (“what ideas do I have about X”, “list my ideas”, “show the idea about Y”, “research that idea deeper”, “that one is promising”, “park that idea”), or asks whether anything they have been working on relates to their ideas (“is any of my recent work related to my ideas”, “anything in my ideas worth doing now”), typically during spare token budget. Ideas are stored in a local folder or a private git repository, never in the current project.

```bash
gh skill install addaix/ideadump ideadump --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`ideadump/data/skills/ideadump`](https://github.com/addaix/ideadump/tree/HEAD/ideadump/data/skills/ideadump) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install ideadump`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/addaix/ideadump/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://addaix.github.io/ideadump/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`ideadump.md`](https://addaix.github.io/ideadump/ideadump.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://addaix.github.io/ideadump/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
